clue.text: On Friday, anything makes one tense

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything at all

explanation.surface: Someone finds that anything happening on a Friday puts them on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraught situation or person is anxious and strained, full of nervous tension.

clue.text: I get close, within foot, of painting

indicators.note: the next pieces sit inside the abbreviation for foot

parts.note: to get close is to near

explanation.surface: Someone approaches an artwork, standing within a foot of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting is one of the fine arts, the visual arts valued for beauty.

clue.text: Can I be friendly?

parts.note: am is a form of the verb to be
can means to be able

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are capable of being sociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can I be' rephrased is 'Am I able', so the pieces come in a different order from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An amiable person is good-natured and pleasant, warmly sociable.

clue.text: In poor motels, I go very miserable

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Staying in shabby motels leaves someone deeply depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomiest is the superlative of gloomy, most dejected or dismal.

clue.text: Worst possible place to refuel car?

explanation.surface: Describes a terrible spot for filling up a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang idiom for something awful, and in motor racing the service area beside the track where cars refuel.

clue.text: Give up hope of being wildly praised

indicators.note: acting wildly, the letters of the next word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone loses heart after receiving extravagant praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all expectation that things will improve.

clue.text: Showing no emotion as late nap disturbed

parts.note: the late means someone dead

indicators.note: the letters of the short sleep are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone woken from a late snooze shows no feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face or manner is expressionless and impassive.

clue.text: Change dress

explanation.surface: Someone is told to alter their clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To move or alter is one sense; the other is a simple loose-fitting garment for women.

clue.text: Flavouring has a Belfast origin

parts.note: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, NI
a seed is the origin from which something grows

explanation.surface: Some food flavouring is said to have come from Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant gives a liquorice taste used in cooking and drinks.

clue.text: Socialists wouldn't govern so fairly

explanation.surface: Left-wing politicians would never rule in a just way.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense punningly means in a right-wing way, which socialists on the left would avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling from the right is what socialists avoid, and the word also means justly or correctly.

clue.text: The best a few find offensive

parts.note: the best is number one, abbreviated NO. 1, read as NOI
a few means some

explanation.surface: A small group finds the top choice distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The best' is No. 1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noisome is foul-smelling or disgusting, so it causes offence.

clue.text: A revolt is occurring

parts.note: a rising is a rebellion or revolt

explanation.surface: A news line announces that a rebellion is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arising is coming into being, happening now.

clue.text: Book of stamps?

parts.note: suggests a ledger of official rubber stamps, but means the volume a collector mounts postage stamps in

explanation.definitionFit: A collector keeps a philatelic collection in a bound volume made for the purpose.

clue.text: I am in hospital, fretting

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
someone in hospital is a patient

explanation.surface: A hospitalised person admits to being restless and worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' as a noun here contrasts with the adjective it forms the opposite of.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fretting is restless and unable to wait calmly, the opposite of calm forbearance.

clue.text: Dissertations about universal Greek hero

indicators.note: the dissertations go around, about, the next letter

parts.note: dissertations are theses
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Academic papers discuss a legendary figure of Greece with universal appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian king who slew the Minotaur is a legendary hero of Greek myth.

clue.text: Ken and lady writhing in the nude

indicators.note: writhing twists about, so the letters of the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man and a woman wriggle about without any clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in the nude means doing it without clothing, unclothed.

clue.text: One abducting child taken to head

parts.note: a kid is a child
napper is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: A child is brought to see the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seizes a person and holds them, often for ransom, abducts them.

clue.text: Talked about having headgear

parts.note: C, from circa, is the abbreviation for about
having a hat on means hatted

explanation.surface: People discussed someone who was wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To have chatted is to have spoken informally, conversed.

clue.text: Clear the stage prepare to sail

explanation.surface: Actors leave as a ship gets ready to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre terms, removing actors or getting rid of something; at sea, untying a boat's moorings.

clue.text: A daughter chose to be separated from parents

parts.note: opted means chose

explanation.surface: A daughter decided to leave her mother and father.
explanation.definitionFit: A child taken into another family's legal care has been parted from birth parents.

clue.text: Out of one's depth here in river-wait

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
pend means to wait, hang in suspense

explanation.surface: Someone struggles in a river where they had to wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown in the place where the water is over your head is an idiom for facing difficulty unprepared.

clue.text: Spinster is game

explanation.surface: Describes an unmarried woman as a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned term for an unmarried older woman, and also a card game where players avoid being left with the odd queen.

clue.text: Not the Shetlands, nor Skye, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly means turned out unexpectedly, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The islands meant are neither the Shetlands nor Skye, to someone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The other northern Scottish island group, next to but distinct from Shetland.

clue.text: Middle Easterner had a lot of night's entertainment

definitions.text: had a lot of night's entertainment

explanation.surface: A man from the Gulf enjoyed many evenings of stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense alludes to the Arabian Nights, the thousand-and-one tales told night after night.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Arabia, and the adjective of the Arabian Nights, a famous story collection told over a thousand nights.

clue.text: Merit of French verse in translation

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: translated, the letters of the poem word are rendered in new order

explanation.surface: A French poem's worth is judged in translation.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to have earned it, to merit it.

clue.text: Unexpected test for measles?

parts.note: a surprise inspection, playfully read as checking skin for the red dots of measles

explanation.definitionFit: A random inspection without warning, punningly a check for the rash of spots.

clue.text: Cold: I'll put central heating on

explanation.surface: Feeling cold, someone resolves to turn the heating on.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a cold feeling or a mild feverish cold.

clue.text: Get together my confession of stupidity

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to foolishness while gathering things.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as AM ASS: 'I am an ass'.
explanation.definitionFit: To accumulate or gather is one sense; split in two, the letters say 'am ass', admitting to being a fool.

clue.text: In summary, it's unpopular to queue

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion, unpopular
a line is a queue of people

explanation.surface: A brief statement says that standing in queues has fallen out of favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief sketch giving the main points is a synopsis or summary.

clue.text: More spacious per item repacked

indicators.note: the letters are packed again in a different order

explanation.surface: Each article packed again leaves more room in a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptier means with less in it, so having more free room.

clue.text: Toyed absent-mindedly with violin?

parts.note: fiddling idly with something, and also playing a fiddle, the violin

explanation.definitionFit: To play idly with an object, and the instrument nicknamed a fiddle suggests playing it.

clue.text: Unfamiliar way to the mountains

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A route leading to the mountains is one we do not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange is odd or not known before, unfamiliar.
